notes: B1 Parity: the Panel not-installed gate is marked platform-only, but Linux does not have it. .claude/agents_shared/shell_parity/windows.md:46 (SPW-042) labels the whole row platform-only. Its stated reason covers only the elevation wait (ts_restart_service), the help default and the ImagePath parsing. The row also records the new Show-TailscalePanel gate at TailscaleCommon.ps1:491-495, where 'not installed' now means the not-installed message and nothing opens. Linux has no such gate: scripts/shells/linux/common/tailscale_common.sh:311-334 ts_show_panel prints both URLs and calls ts_open_url on the admin console whether or not Tailscale is installed. It never calls is_tailscale_installed before that open, and it never says the tool is not installed. The user's D29 wording scopes restart, panel and devices to 'if installed', and Windows follows it, so the divergence is real and belongs to Linux. The comment at TailscaleCommon.ps1:483-485 is also false: it says ts_show_panel 'gates opening them the same way'. The report and result say 'No pending-linux row was left open', which hides this gap from the orchestrator. -> Split the Panel part out of SPW-042 into its own row, either: (a) pending-linux, with this exact counterpart request: 'tailscale_common.sh ts_show_panel: when ! is_tailscale_installed, print the not-installed notice (pointing at 97_install_tailscale.sh / the menu Install entry) and return before printing or opening any panel'; the orchestrator must then open a [shell-linux] align task in TASKS.md; or (b) a genuine platform-only reason that covers the Panel behavior. Then fix or remove the comment at TailscaleCommon.ps1:483-485 so it describes the Linux behavior correctly, and fix the 'No pending-linux row' line in the report.
non_blocking:
Dot-source side effects are still open. This was already flagged in the shell-windows-9 r2 note 'for shell-windows-10'. The comment at FrankenPhpManager.ps1:9-13 says dot-sourcing is 'safe', but it is not:
- The param block at TailscaleCommon.ps1:28-36 runs in each caller's scope. A pre-existing $Action is silently reset to ''. When no $Action exists yet, the new $Action/$PanelTarget variables keep the [string] and [ValidateSet] attributes, so a later script-level `$Action = 'x'` throws: 'The variable cannot be validated because the value x is not a valid value'. I verified this in a scratch PS 5.1 test.
- TailscaleCommon.ps1:40 now loads the 3292-line CommonFunc.ps1 into every FrankenPhpManager consumer that never loaded it: Step93/94/96/175, FrankenPhpCertificateManager, and both start.ps1 files. That includes the [Console]::OutputEncoding and $OutputEncoding UTF8 side effects.
- Nothing breaks today. Checked: no case-insensitive $action/$panelTarget at an affected scope; FrankenPhpCertificateManager.ps1:301 `$action =` is function-local, and a scratch test shows it gets a fresh variable; no function-name collisions with CommonFunc or TailscaleCommon.
-> Split the file into a param-less library (constants plus Find/Get functions) that FrankenPhpManager dot-sources, and a thin -Action entry. Or at least correct the 'safe' comment.

FrankenPhpManager.ps1:750 `& $tailscaleExe status 2>&1 | Out-Null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0)` is a third, exit-code-based status probe (pre-existing at 74e7770:733). Under the EAP=Stop set by GlobalVars, a stopped daemon's stderr throws NativeCommandError in PS 5.1 (the same behavior as shell-windows-G2 B1), so the [MANUAL] warning never prints. The spec also prefers BackendState over exit codes. -> Reuse `(Get-TailscaleStatusSummary -TailscaleExe $tailscaleExe).BackendState -ne $script:TailscaleRunningState` while the dedup is open.

TailscaleCommon.ps1:457: after `Start-Process -Verb RunAs -Wait`, the message is always -Type 'Success', even if the elevated Restart-Service failed and the status read back is Stopped. -> Choose Success or Warning from $afterStatus.Status.

The same capture carries an unreported comment-only hunk at FrankenPhpManager.ps1:29-32, which removes the reference to the D7 hand-written 50-d7-local-extensions.ini. It is harmless, but the report does not list it.
